title: The equations of a relative global complete intersection form a regular sequence at every prime
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\ge0$ integers, $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in P$ such that $S=P/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak q'\subset P$ its inverse image under the quotient map $P\to S$ (a prime ideal containing $f_1,\dots,f_c$), and let $P_{\mathfrak q'}$ be the localization of $P$ at $\mathfrak q'$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ is a regular sequence in the local ring $P_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal, line 36767), part (1), with its proof (lines 36786-36832: the Noetherian case by Lemma 00SC lemma-lci and Lemma 00MG lemma-grothendieck-regular-sequence, the general case by absolute Noetherian approximation, Lemma 00SU, Lemma 05UU lemma-colimit-rings-flat and Lemma 00DB lemma-directed-colimit-exact); tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00SV,algebra-lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal)

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak p=R\cap\mathfrak q'$ and $B=P_{\mathfrak q'}$. First assume $R$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The monomials form an $R$-basis of $P$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], so $P$ is flat over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. The polynomial ring $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] the induced map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to B$ is a flat local map of Noetherian local rings. Its closed-fibre ring is $B/\mathfrak pB$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal), lines 36783-36792, first paragraph; flat localization is Lemma Tag 00HT (6)

proof.text: Still assuming $R$ Noetherian, set $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $C=P\otimes_Rk$. The base-change isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] identifies $C$ with $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and sends $f_j\otimes1$ to the coefficientwise images $\bar f_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection], $\mathfrak q'$ determines a prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $C$ contracting to $\mathfrak q'$; let $\mathfrak q''$ be its image in $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. Base change [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-base-change] makes $T=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)$ a relative global complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. The prime $\mathfrak q''$ contains all $\bar f_j$, so $T\ne0$ and its sole fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has dimension $n-c$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence] applies at $\mathfrak q''$ and says that the $\bar f_j/1$ are regular in $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_{\mathfrak q''}$. The explicit isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-local-ring-natural-iso] identifies this ring with $B/\mathfrak pB$ and sends the class of $f_j/1$ to $\bar f_j/1$; hence the images of the $f_j/1$ form a regular sequence in $B/\mathfrak pB$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SV, lines 36785-36792 ('By Lemma 00SC ... regular sequence in ... tensor_R kappa(p)'); Lemma Tag 00SC (lemma-lci), last paragraph, and Remark Tag 0H9M for the fibre local ring

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-regular-sequence-flat] now hold for the flat local map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to B$ from step 1 and its closed fibre $B/\mathfrak pB$ from step 2: both local rings are Noetherian and the fibre images of $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ are regular. The lemma gives that $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ is a regular sequence in $B$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. This establishes the claim for Noetherian $R$; it includes $c=0$, since $B$ is a nonzero local ring at the prime $\mathfrak q'$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SV, lines 36789-36793, application of Lemma Tag 00MG (lemma-grothendieck-regular-sequence) to obtain assertion (1)

proof.text: Now let $R$ be arbitrary. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-noetherian-approximation], choose a finite type $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra $R_0\subseteq R$ containing the coefficients of all $f_j$ such that $S_0=R_0[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection. Let $\Lambda$ be the directed set of subrings $R_\lambda\subseteq R$ generated as rings by $R_0$ and finitely many further elements of $R$. Their union is $R$. Each $R_\lambda$ is a finite type $\mathbf Z$-algebra, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and $S_\lambda=R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection by [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-base-change]. Set $P_\lambda=R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and $\mathfrak q'_\lambda=\mathfrak q'\cap P_\lambda$; this is prime, contains all $f_j$, and therefore determines a prime of $S_\lambda$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SV, lines 36795-36813: finite type Z-subalgebras containing the R_0 of Lemma Tag 00SU and base change by Lemma Tag 00SS

proof.text: For each $\lambda$, put $B_\lambda=(P_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q'_\lambda}$. Step 3 applies to the Noetherian ring $R_\lambda$, the relative global complete intersection $S_\lambda$ and its prime induced by $\mathfrak q'$, so $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ is regular in $B_\lambda$. The inclusions $P_\lambda\subseteq P_\mu\subseteq P$ and the identities $\mathfrak q'_\lambda=\mathfrak q'_\mu\cap P_\lambda$ give compatible localization maps $B_\lambda\to B_\mu\to B$. Every fraction $h/s\in B$ has $h,s\in P_\lambda$ for some $\lambda$, with $s\notin\mathfrak q'_\lambda$, and hence comes from $B_\lambda$. If a fraction from $B_\lambda$ maps to zero in $B$, some $u\in P\setminus\mathfrak q'$ kills its numerator; enlarging $\lambda$ to contain the finitely many coefficients of $u$ makes it zero already in $B_\mu$. Thus $B=\varinjlim B_\lambda$. The same finite-coefficient argument, applied also to coefficients of expressions in $(f_1,\dots,f_i)B$, gives $B/(f_1,\dots,f_i)B=\varinjlim B_\lambda/(f_1,\dots,f_i)B_\lambda$ for every $0\le i\le c$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SV, lines 36813-36829: the displayed colimit of localized quotients; the fraction criterion spells out its identification

proof.text: For $0\le i<c$, multiplication by $f_{i+1}/1$ on $B_\lambda/(f_1,\dots,f_i)B_\lambda$ is injective, by regularity in step 5 [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]; these multiplication maps form a compatible system. By exactness of filtered colimits [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] and the quotient identifications in step 5, multiplication by $f_{i+1}/1$ on $B/(f_1,\dots,f_i)B$ is injective. Finally $B/(f_1,\dots,f_c)B$ is the localization of $S=P/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ at its prime $\mathfrak q$, hence is nonzero: its maximal ideal is proper [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. These are precisely the two conditions of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], so $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ is regular in $B=P_{\mathfrak q'}$.
